findings.description: Castro Nail Salon reopened at 4359 18th Street (at Eureka Street) on Friday, September 18, after being forced to vacate its longtime space in the building shared with the historic Castro Theatre earlier in the year. The new space was remodeled over the spring with new plumbing, electrical, an ADA bathroom, chairs and paint at an estimated construction cost of $97,000; it was previously home to Big Cleaners, which closed in August 2020. The reopening was delayed while the landlord permitted an ADU added to the ground floor.

citation.label: Hoodline, “Castro Nail Salon Settles into New Location After Move,” 19 September 2026

findings.description: L'Amourette Chocolat, a San Francisco chocolate maker, will open a new chocolate shop and cafe at 548 Castro Street in the former plant shop How's It Hanging, offering chocolates, confections and espresso/coffee in an Art Deco-influenced interior. No opening date had been announced and no construction permits or planning applications had been filed at publication. It would be the company's second San Francisco shop after its Pacific Heights location at 2412 Fillmore Street (opened 2022).

findings.description: San Francisco health inspectors closed Corgi Insurance's Dogpatch cafe at 2146 Third Street on September 16 after finding it operating without a valid health permit; an official notice was posted at the entrance. The 24/7 cafe had opened recently as the company's second San Francisco location; the company characterized the problem as a permitting transition, saying it had operated under a temporary permit while seeking a permanent one. The cafe remained closed at publication.

findings.description: Lincoln Property Company and Sabal Investment Holdings acquired the 152,000-square-foot production building at 300 Kansas Street in Showplace Square through a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, after purchasing the underlying debt from Bank of America; the firms secured an $87.9 million first-priority acquisition and lease-up loan from BridgeInvest. Former owner Spear Street Capital reclassified the building as a past asset. The R&D-zoned building is being positioned for hardware, robotics and physical-AI tenants.
